items.title: Israel bombing western Iran to back Kurdish offensive

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Israel backing Iranian Kurdish plans to seize ...

items.description: Israel has been bombing parts of western Iran to support Iranian Kurdish militias preparing to exploit the U.S.-Israeli air war to seize towns along the Iraq-Iran frontier, according to a Reuters exclusive citing three sources familiar with Israel's discussions with the factions. The revelation comes as President Donald Trump told Reuters it would be "wonderful" if Kurdish forces crossed the border into Iran.[1]

items.title: Two new studies show climate crisis worsening faster than projected

featured_image.name: KAIST succeeds in real-time carbon dioxide monitoring ...

items.description: Humanity's annual carbon dioxide emissions now exceed Earth's safe operating limit by more than double, according to a study published in Nature Sustainability and announced by KAIST on March 6. The finding lands amid mounting evidence that the pace of global warming itself is accelerating, with new research placing the current warming rate at levels unseen in the modern instrumental record.

items.title: Iceland sets Aug. 29 referendum on resuming EU talks

featured_image.name: Parliament House, Reykjavik, Iceland, 2013 | This stone buil… | Flickr

items.description: Iceland's government announced on Friday that it will hold a national referendum on August 29 on whether to resume talks to join the European Union, accelerating a pledge to put the question to voters by 2027 amid mounting geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Russia sharing intelligence with Iran to target US forces, officials say

featured_image.name: Russia, Iran sign military cooperation deal

items.description:
Russia has been providing Iran with targeting information on American military assets in the Middle East since the war erupted on February 28, according to a Washington Post report citing three U.S. officials familiar with the intelligence. The assistance includes real-time data on the locations of U.S. warships and aircraft, marking the first indication that another major American adversary is indirectly involved in the conflict.[1]

"It does seem like it's a pretty comprehensive effort," one official told the Washington Post.[2][3]

items.title: Iran war costs nearly $900M a day as oil hits 2-year high

featured_image.name: Oil prices surge because of Iran war : NPR

items.description: One week into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, oil prices have climbed to their highest levels in nearly two years, rattling global markets and raising urgent questions about the economic toll of a widening Middle East conflict. Brent crude surged roughly 25% from pre-war levels to trade near $85 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate rose to the upper $70s, as Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz choked off a shipping lane that carries about 20% of the world's oil supply.[1][2][3]

items.title: Hungary detains Ukrainian bank staff, seizes cash and gold in convoy

featured_image.name: Hungary hides stolen Oschadbank armored vehicles carrying ...

items.description: Hungarian authorities detained seven employees of Ukraine's state-owned Oschadbank on March 5 and seized two armored vehicles carrying $40 million, €35 million, and 9 kilograms of gold, triggering a furious response from Kyiv and marking a dramatic escalation in the feud between the two countries over Russian oil transit.

items.title: Axel Springer agrees to buy UK's Telegraph for £575M

featured_image.name: RedBird Secures $675M Deal To Buy UK's Daily Telegraph - Deadline

items.description: German media publisher Axel Springer has agreed to buy Britain's Telegraph Media Group for £575 million, according to a report in the Financial Times, in a move that scuttles the proposed acquisition by the Daily Mail's owner and places one of Britain's oldest newspapers under German ownership for the first time in its 168-year history.[1][2]

items.title: Trump demands 'unconditional surrender' as Iran war enters Day 7

featured_image.name: Trump says there will be no deal with Iran except 'unconditional surrender'

items.description:
The US-Israeli military campaign against Iran showed no signs of abating on March 6, 2026, as Israel launched heavy airstrikes on Tehran and Beirut overnight while Iran continued retaliatory strikes on Israel, American military bases, and Gulf state capitals. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the conflict has "only just commenced," while President Trump declared on Truth Social that there would be "no deal with Iran except UNCONDITIONAL SURRENDER".[1][2]

The war, now in its seventh day, has killed more than 1,000 civilians in Iran alone, according to the US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency, which reported 1,097 civilian deaths including 181 children under the age of 10. An Iranian government agency put the overall death toll inside the country above 1,200 as of March 5. Six US service members have been killed, all in a single Iranian strike on a base in Kuwait, along with at least 12 in Israel, 123 in Lebanon, and dozens more across Gulf states.[3][4][5][6][7][8]

items.title: Study finds global warming rate nearly doubled since 2015

featured_image.name: Studie: Globale Erwärmung beschleunigt sich seit gut zehn Jahren massiv

items.description: Two studies released this week paint a stark picture of accelerating climate threats: sea levels along the world's coasts are already far higher than most research assumed, and the rate of global warming has nearly doubled over the past decade.

items.title: China to power up world's first accelerator-driven nuclear reactor in 2027

featured_image.name: China is building world-first triad reactor system to power ...

items.description: China is preparing to power up the world's first megawatt-level accelerator-driven subcritical reactor, a device its developers say can burn uranium 100 times more efficiently than conventional reactors while reducing the lifespan of nuclear waste to less than a thousandth of current levels.

items.title: Hungary seizes Ukrainian bank vehicles amid oil pipeline crisis with Kyiv

featured_image.name: Hungary hides stolen Oschadbank armored vehicles carrying ...

items.description: A rapidly intensifying diplomatic crisis between Hungary and Ukraine erupted into open hostility this week after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy suggested he could give Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban's address to Ukrainian soldiers, prompting Budapest to condemn the remark as a death threat. The confrontation, centered on Hungary's blocking of a €90 billion EU loan to Ukraine and a dispute over the Druzhba oil pipeline, escalated further on March 5 when Hungary seized Ukrainian state bank vehicles carrying tens of millions of dollars in cash and gold.

items.title: UK arrests four men suspected of spying on Jewish sites for Iran

featured_image.name: UK police arrest seven Iranians over alleged threats to national security

items.description:
British counter-terrorism police arrested four men early Friday on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service by conducting surveillance of locations and individuals linked to London's Jewish community, the Metropolitan Police said in a statement.[1]

The suspects — one Iranian national and three dual British-Iranian citizens — were detained shortly after 1 a.m. at addresses in Barnet and Watford as part of a pre-planned operation. They were arrested under section 3 of the National Security Act 2023, which criminalizes assisting a foreign intelligence service. "The country to which the investigation relates is Iran," the Met confirmed.[1]

items.title: Kuwait cuts oil output as storage fills amid Hormuz blockade

featured_image.name: Kuwait Cuts Oil Production as Storage Fills Up

items.description: Kuwait has begun reducing oil production at several of its fields after running out of room to store crude that cannot be exported through the blocked Strait of Hormuz, The Wall Street Journal reported in an exclusive on Thursday. The move marks the latest escalation in a widening storage crisis threatening to knock millions of barrels of Gulf oil off global markets.[1]

items.title: Sri Lanka evacuates second Iranian warship after US sub sinks frigate

featured_image.name: Sri Lanka takes control of second Iranian vessel a day after US sinks  warship

items.description:
Sri Lanka rescued 32 Iranian sailors and evacuated 208 crew members from a second Iranian naval vessel this week after a U.S. submarine torpedoed and sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena off the island's southern coast, killing 87 people in what marked the first torpedo sinking of an enemy warship by the U.S. Navy since World War II.

The Moudge-class frigate was struck approximately 40 nautical miles off Galle early on March 4, while returning to Iran from a multinational naval exercise hosted by India in the Bay of Bengal. U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed the attack, calling it a "quiet death" and describing the IRIS Dena as a "prize ship".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: European stocks rise as oil eases after sharpest weekly surge since 2022

featured_image.name: European stocks to open higher amid easing oil price, Iran war

items.description: Global financial markets entered Friday on uncertain footing as the escalating conflict between the United States and Israel on one side and Iran on the other continued to roil energy markets and rattle investor confidence. European stocks opened higher on Friday as oil prices eased slightly from their sharpest weekly surge since 2022, according to CNBC, though Asian equities largely fell amid persistent concerns over supply disruptions and inflation.[1]

items.title: Asian markets mixed as Iran conflict enters 7th day

featured_image.name: Asian shares are mixed in cautious trading after a mixed day on Wall Street

items.description: Financial markets capped a turbulent week on Friday as Asian shares traded mixed and oil prices edged lower, offering a brief reprieve from the volatile swings that have rattled investors since the United States and Israel launched joint military strikes on Iran on February 28. The conflict, now in its seventh day, has closed the Strait of Hormuz, disrupted global energy supplies, and sent shockwaves through every major asset class.

items.title: Israel launches 'broad-scale' strikes on Tehran, Beirut

featured_image.name: Tehran says Israeli fighter jets used US-controlled airspace over Iraq to attack  Iran as death

items.description:
Israel unleashed what it called a "broad-scale wave of strikes" on Tehran and carried out 26 airstrikes on southern Beirut early Friday as the war across the Middle East entered its seventh day, with U.S. officials warning that the bombardment was about to intensify further.

The Israel Defense Forces said overnight that it had begun targeting "Iranian terror regime infrastructure in Tehran," posting about the operation on Telegram just after 4 a.m. local time. Observers on the ground described the strikes as the heaviest yet on the Iranian capital, with explosions shaking residential neighborhoods, the area around Tehran University, and a military academy. Al Jazeera's correspondent in Tehran reported "a relentless series of massive strikes" accompanied by fighter jets and thick smoke.[1][2][3]

items.title: Oil retreats as US weighs futures market action

featured_image.name: Markets News, March 5, 2026: U.S. Indexes Tumble as Oil Hits $80 a Barrel; Dow Closes Down Almost 800 Points

items.description:
Markets around the world lurched through another volatile session on Thursday as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its seventh day, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average briefly plunging more than 1,000 points before oil prices pulled back from their highs on reports of possible US government intervention in futures markets.

The Dow shed 784 points, or 1.6%, closing at 47,954.74, according to The Wall Street Journal, after US crude surged past $80 a barrel for the first time since summer 2024. The S&P 500 fell 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.3%, reversing a Wednesday rally that had been fueled by reports Iran was open to indirect negotiations with Washington.[1][2][3]

items.title: Physicists create first computer model of 'ideal glass'

featured_image.name: Scientists open new window on the physics of glass formation

items.description: A team of physicists at the University of Oregon has created the first computer model of an "ideal glass," a long-theorized material in which molecules are packed as tightly and stably as possible while maintaining the disordered, amorphous structure that defines glass. The achievement, published in Physical Review Letters, addresses a challenge first posed nearly eight decades ago and could eventually reshape how advanced materials are designed and manufactured.[1][2]

items.title: Cambridge scientists discover 'molecular catapult' in solar materials

featured_image.name: Molecular 'catapult' fires electrons at the limits of physics

items.description: Scientists at the University of Cambridge have observed electrons crossing the boundary between solar materials in just 18 femtoseconds — less than 20 quadrillionths of a second — propelled by molecular vibrations acting as a "catapult." The discovery, published March 5 in Nature Communications, challenges decades of assumptions about how charge moves through solar energy systems and could reshape the design of more efficient light-harvesting technologies.[1][2]
